clue.text: Aladdin's light?

parts.note: Aladdin's lamp housed a genie, a spirit, so his light is a lamp with a spirit in it, though the real thing burns methylated spirit

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun: the device is a lamp that burns alcohol, and Aladdin's lamp held a genie.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burner fuelled by methylated alcohol is the everyday name, punned on the genie in the famous lamp.

clue.text: Left hole in side

explanation.definitionFit: The left side of a ship is its port, and a porthole is a window opening in the ship's side.

clue.text: Painter is fashionable, old fruit

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword painter
taken as written
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: An artist is in vogue while eating stale fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fruit is a grape that has been left to age and shrivel.

clue.text: First lady in this honourable membership

indicators.note: the first lady is placed inside the word this

parts.note: taken as written
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The President's wife belongs to this respectable club.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'honour among thieves': a band of crooks is a membership with its own code of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'honour among thieves' makes a gang of robbers an ironically honourable fellowship.

clue.text: Help with a Verdi production

parts.note: to aid is to help
taken as written

explanation.surface: Assistance is given in staging an opera by Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi composed this opera about an Ethiopian princess, first staged in Cairo.

clue.text: Colour of FBI agents in coalmine

indicators.note: the agents are placed inside the coalmine

parts.note: a pit is a coalmine
G-men are American government agents of the FBI

explanation.surface: Federal agents are spotted underground in a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, as in paint.

clue.text: Epigram can be twisted to describe old soldier

indicators.note: twisting the letters of the two words rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A witty saying can be distorted to portray a veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran who has served in many military expeditions is called an old campaigner.

clue.text: Transparency firmly fixed there is no flaw in it

definitions.text: there is no flaw in it

parts.note: water is the clarity or lustre of a gem, as in 'a diamond of the first water'
tight means firmly fixed

explanation.surface: A clear slide fastened securely has no defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transparency' looks like a slide or overhead sheet, but here it is the jeweller's 'water', the clarity of a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument or alibi described as watertight has no gap or weakness anywhere.

clue.text: Students' celebration with a piece of Indian music

parts.note: rag is the British university students' charity carnival
taken as written

explanation.surface: Undergraduates party with a bit of Indian melody.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is a British student tradition of charity stunts and parades.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework used for improvisation in classical Indian music.

clue.text: Marmot — plain barker

parts.note: a prairie is a grassy plain
a dog is an animal that barks

explanation.surface: A marmot is described as an unremarkable yapper.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American burrowing rodent, related to the marmot, gives a bark-like alarm call.

clue.text: Confused epigram right out gets the bird

indicators.note: the letters of the saying are muddled once the right is taken out

explanation.surface: A muddled witticism without the correct word earns a jeering reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right out' says the R is taken from EPIGRAM; 'Confused' rearranges the letters left, EPIGAM. 'gets the bird' suggests being booed, but 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white member of the crow family.

clue.text: Repairer takes in a fret pattern that is intricate

indicators.note: the repairer word swallows the letter a inside it

parts.note: a mender repairs things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tradesman fixing a guitar works on a complicated fret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fret' suggests a guitar, but a fret is also a geometric border of interlocking lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek key border of winding right-angled lines is called a meander, after the twisting river.

clue.text: Pitman of Wrekin more unsteady

indicators.note: unsteady letters wobble out of order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coal miner from the Wrekin area is less steady on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wrekin is a hill in Shropshire, England, near the old coalfields.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitman is a man who labours down a coal pit.

clue.text: He knocks down lots of people

definitions.text: He knocks down lots of people

parts.words: He knocks down lots of people
parts.note: read as violence, but knocking down is the fall of a hammer at a sale, and lots are items for bidders

explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks down' and 'lots' look like assault on a crowd; at a sale the gavel 'knocks down' each lot to a buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running a sale room brings down the hammer to sell each lot.

clue.text: Lorelei's home — throw her in

indicators.note: throw suggests tossing the letters about to land in a new order

explanation.surface: Dump the siren into the river where she lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is the legendary siren of a rock on the German river.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places the siren on a rock above this German river, luring boatmen to wreck.

clue.text: Is it man, perhaps, who has a soul? Not entirely, I say

definitions.text: who has a soul? Not entirely, I say

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A speaker doubts that humans alone possess a soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the believer's answer to the question: not only humans, since in this belief every object and creature has a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Animism holds that spirits dwell in animals, plants and objects, not in people alone.

clue.text: Sit up with a story from him?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word for sit is read from the bottom

parts.note: to pose is to sit for a portrait

explanation.surface: Stay awake with a bedtime tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns POSE into ESOP; 'Sit up' looks like staying awake, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist is the source of many moral tales.

clue.text: Paper shows these changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of these are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on current alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single piece of paper.

clue.text: Stir in some tonic kelp

indicators.note: in some says the answer is part of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Mix a little seaweed into a health drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a verb for mixing, but it is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for prison, as in 'doing time in the nick'.

clue.text: Sheltered from firearms' recoil?

indicators.note: recoil means spring back, so the word for firearms is read backwards

parts.note: guns are firearms

explanation.surface: Protected from the kick of rifles.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug spot is cosy and protected from wind and weather.

clue.text: Sneak about to find love in tin-work

indicators.note: the love letter goes inside the tin and work pair

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
op is short for opus, a work
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A burglar creeps around looking for romance in a metalwork shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To snoop is to pry or nose around secretly.

clue.text: Prejudiced and lets free

indicators.note: free says the letters are released from their order to form a new word

explanation.surface: A biased judge releases a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanted report is biased, tilted toward one side.

clue.text: Wide-mouthed baseballer?

parts.note: reads as a big-mouthed player, but combines the jug with a broad lip and the player who throws the ball

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses are fused in one picture: the large jug with a wide lip and the baseball player who throws to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug with a lip is named the same as the player on the mound who throws.

clue.text: Cut wood thus, having tiniest bit let loose

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: let loose sets those three letters free to rearrange

explanation.surface: A carver shaves wood, releasing the smallest chips.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve wood by paring off small shavings with a knife is to whittle.

clue.text: Performer to talk nonsense on jetty

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the jetty word

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
to rot is to talk rubbish

explanation.surface: A seaside entertainer babbles on the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: The French clown in white costume is a stage performer of pantomime and seaside shows.

clue.text: Metrical stresses needing no vowels

parts.note: the pattern of beats in verse, spelt without any of the five vowels

explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic part points to the word's spelling: Y does the vowel's work, so none of A, E, I, O, U is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The regular pattern of beats in poetry or music goes by this name.

clue.text: Single over there that writer about Broadway characters

parts.note: a single in cricket is one run
yon is an old word for that one over there

explanation.surface: A lone figure over there writes about New York theatre people.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon Runyon wrote stories of New York gamblers and gangsters, the basis of Guys and Dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon wrote short stories about the colourful street life of New York's theatre district.

clue.text: Old lament found in pile of rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: A dump was an old mournful song, the source of 'down in the dumps', and a tip for waste.

clue.text: Article appearing soon

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
on means appearing, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A newspaper story is coming out shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Judging standard of jasper?

explanation.definitionFit: A criterion for testing quality, named after the black jasper stone once used to test gold by its streak.

clue.text: 206 employed in Jug brewery

indicators.note: employed in says the jug works inside the word brewery, as part of its letters

explanation.surface: A jug is put to use at a beer works.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, traditionally for washing water.

clue.text: Manners to transport chaps on time

parts.note: to deport is to transport out of the country
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Etiquette demands the punctual removal of the men.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is a person's bearing and behaviour.
